chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Muhammad ibn Ali from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Umar was brought a woman whose husband was an old man. When he had intercourse with her, he died on her body. She gave birth to a child, and his sons claimed she had committed fornication and testified against her. Umar ordered that she be stoned.
Ali (peace be upon him) passed by her, and she said, 'O son of the cousin of the Messenger of Allah, I have a proof.' He said, 'Bring your proof.'
She handed him a letter, and he read it. He said, 'This woman informs you of the day she married him and the day he had intercourse with her, how his intercourse with her was. Return the woman.'
When it was the next day, he called for young boys of similar age and called for the infant with them. He said to them, 'Play,' until play distracted them, then he said to them, 'Sit.'
They sat until they were settled. He called out to them, and the boys stood up. The young boy stood up and leaned on his palms. Ali (peace be upon him) called for him.
He made him inherit from his father and lashed his brothers with the punishment of the disputant. Umar said to him, 'What did you do?'
He said, 'I recognized the weakness of the old man in the boy leaning on his palms.'
ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali use observation of a child to determine the cause of an old man's death in marital relations?
ai.summary: This narrative from Tahdhib al-Ahkam illustrates the Imam’s use of 'ilm al-alamah (knowledge of signs) and practical deduction to establish legal truth, a method highly valued in Shia jurisprudence for resolving evidentiary gaps. By observing a child’s natural posture, Ali (AS) inferred the physical limitations of the elderly husband, thereby distinguishing natural death from the wife’s alleged infidelity and saving her from stoning. This incident highlights the Shia emphasis on rational observation and contextual understanding within the broader framework of judicial evidence.
